report:
A–D hold, and the current article and complete n1–n4 dependency chain establish the original restricted sufficient-condition alternative. The result covers every member of the specified smooth Hessian family and every original exact maximizer, with uniform positive bounds for both density normalizations. This assessment does not rely on earlier PASS verdicts, candidate flags, hashes, reading receipts, or symbolic diagnostics.

Gauduchon’s general Theorem 2 applies. Its index-zero/maximum-principle argument gives a one-dimensional adjoint kernel; orthogonality excludes a sign-changing generator, and the positivity corollary excludes zeros. Connectedness, compactness and smooth positivity hold. The even-Betti condition belongs to Theorem 1; the dd^c rescaling preserves closedness. [Primary text](https://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf).

For B, write Q=σ^(n−1), where δh≤σ=h+dd^c v≤Λh. Integrability gives dσ=dh and d^cσ=d^ch. Consequently dQ=(n−1)dh∧σ^(n−2) and d^cQ=(n−1)d^ch∧σ^(n−2). These identities cancel the varying third derivatives. The supplemental identity in n2 also has the correct sign: dd^cQ=(n−1)dd^ch∧σ^(n−2)+(n−1)(n−2)dh∧d^ch∧σ^(n−3).

Both cofactor conventions agree. In a fixed holomorphic chart with constant positive coordinate volume Ω, define A and b by insertion: ι_(A∇f)Ω=d^cf∧Q and ι_bΩ=d^cQ. Then dd^c(ρQ)=0 is exactly div(A∇ρ+bρ)=0. The rank-one positive-form identity makes A real symmetric and gives δ^(n−1)A_h≤A≤Λ^(n−1)A_h. The expression for d^cQ bounds b using only fixed torsion and Λ. Thus ellipticity and drift bounds are uniform without coefficient-derivative bounds.

In the article’s convention, n dd^cφ∧Q=J L_σφ dV. Its Stokes signs correctly give P=div_dV(A d)−b·d and P*ρ=div_dV(A dρ+bρ). The type identity dφ∧d^cQ=−d^cφ∧dQ identifies this flux with n times the preceding coordinate flux. Absorbing the fixed volume density preserves uniform coefficient bounds. No estimate of div b is needed.

I independently checked the article’s Harnack proof. Testing the equality by η²ρ^(p−1), for either sign of p−1, and absorbing the three cross terms gives its power-energy bound. Smooth positivity makes every compactly supported negative-power test legitimate individually; no uniform lower bound is assumed. Sobolev applied to ηρ^(p/2) supplies the additional cutoff term, so its iteration factor is bounded by C[1+p²(1+|p−1|^(−2))]. This is an implicit product-rule term, not a substantive repair. The exponents p_j=β^(j−k−1/2), β=2n/(2n−2), avoid one by a fixed dimensional gap. Geometric cutoff losses and polynomial exponent losses have summable logarithms divided by |p_j|. Positive and negative iterations therefore give the claimed supremum and reciprocal-infimum estimates.

The logarithmic test yields ∫η²|∇logρ|²≤C∫(|∇η|²+K²η²). For a subcube of side ℓ, scaling and Poincaré bound mean oscillation by C√(1+K²ℓ²), uniformly. In the supplied dyadic argument, generation j has measure at most a^(−j)|Q| and accumulated oscillation at most (j2^m a+a)K₀. Choosing the exponential coefficient below log(a)/(2^m a) makes the resulting series converge. Hence the product of the positive and negative p₀-moments is uniformly bounded. This completes the article’s Harnack argument without importing John–Nirenberg or assuming a common VMO modulus.

The independent n1–n2 route is also valid. Gilbarg–Trudinger’s operator (8.1), bounds (8.5)–(8.6), and Theorem 8.20 match the equation with real dimension m=2n, c=d=0, principal Frobenius bound √m a₁ and drift parameter b₀/a₀. Smooth positive ρ belongs to the required Sobolev class on relatively compact balls. Theorem 8.20 does not impose condition (8.8). [Authors’ text](https://djvu.online/file/jxRRleAzbYjsl).

Trudinger’s original bounded specialization independently applies: the principal spectral bounds and inverse are bounded, the sector constant is one, and its lower-order quantity is b·A^(−1)b≤b₀²/a₀. Fixed sufficiently large finite s,t satisfy the §5 integrability requirement, and the local quantities in (5.2) are uniformly bounded on the fixed balls. Corollary 5.2 therefore supplies the claimed comparison without coefficient derivatives or a divergence-sign condition. Its operator, structural assumptions and corollary were checked in primary text; screenshot placeholders were not treated as viewed images. [Primary paper](https://www.numdam.org/article/ASNSP_1973_3_27_2_265_0.pdf).

A finite connected overlap cover converts either local proof into sup_Xρ≤H inf_Xρ. Since dV(X)=∫ρ dV=1, H^(−1)≤ρ≤H. This proves B for every smooth potential in its stated quantifier. Qualitative conformal existence alone was not used as a uniform-estimate grant.

For C, set a_v=∫h∧ρσ^(n−1). Smooth dd^c-Stokes gives a_v=∫ρσ^n=∫ρJ dV. Thus T_v=(ρ/a_v)σ^(n−1)=γ_v^(n−1) belongs to the original G_h, with γ_v=(ρ/a_v)^(1/(n−1))σ. The prescribed solution satisfies B₀(F_v)=log c_v and M(F_v)=c_v^(−1/n).

The original trace convention checks exactly. If G is the matrix of γ and s=tr(G^(−1)), then h∧T=(s/n)γ^n and P_T=nG^(−1)/s. Hence det(P_T)^(1/n)(h∧T)=det(G)^((n−1)/n)h^n. There is no extra n or factorial. Consequently k_Tv=(ρ/a_v)J^((n−1)/n), Γ_Fv(T_v)=c_v^(−1/n)(ρJ/a_v)dV, and dν/dV=ρJ/a_v. The alternative determinant-density definition gives the same k_T=J^(−1/n)dν/dV.

This current actually attains M(F_v). Independently, matrix arithmetic–geometric mean gives Γ_Fv(T)≤c_v^(−1/n)σ∧T for every original test current; Stokes gives ∫σ∧T=1. The constructed current attains equality. Task-granted smooth uniqueness then identifies every exact maximizer with T_v; no arbitrary-support identification is imported.

Put j₋=(1−ε₀)^n min_X(h^n/dV) and j₊=(1+ε₀)^n max_X(h^n/dV). Uniformly, j₋≤J,a_v≤j₊. Therefore H^(−1)j₋/j₊≤dν/dV≤Hj₊/j₋ and H^(−1)j₋^((n−1)/n)/j₊≤k_T≤Hj₊^((n−1)/n)/j₋. These prove both critical norms, indeed L∞ bounds. The article’s slightly weaker k-bounds are also valid.

For A, both J_v/J_h and c_v/c₀ lie between (1−ε₀)^n and (1+ε₀)^n. Their logarithmic difference gives exactly the asserted supremum bound. Every F_v is smooth and normalized. The topology is C⁰ supremum norm; compactness, derivative bounds and a common VMO modulus are not assumed.

Both proofs of D work on the original fixed background. In the article, the derivative of F_(tφ) is L_hφ minus its J_h-weighted average. A constant L_hφ must vanish by evaluating at extrema; its zero kernel would force φ constant. A two-point difference therefore becomes strictly monotone for small t. Independently, n3’s supported bump satisfies dd^cw(p)=h(p) and dd^cw(q)=0, giving F_t(p)−F_t(q)=log(J_h(p)/J_h(q))+n log(1+t). Small positive t satisfies the entire family restriction. This distinguishes infinitely many normalized densities, with at most one constant member. Normalization excludes mere constant shifts. Neither construction replaces X or h, nor infers positive lower mass for the unrestricted potential family.

The support DAG is complete: n2 uses n1, n3 is independent, and n4 uses n1–n3. All essential applications and the supplemental differential identity survive reconstruction. Finite symbolic checks do not prove the analytic theorem. The packet’s assertion about an earlier C²α answer or catalogue status is not established here and is not imported into the mathematical conclusion.

The entire current-versus-original source change is the harmless c_v/c₀ notation clarification: variable mass is c_v, while c₀ denotes v=0. No substantial repair is required. The supplied review’s passages 4–6 literally carry premise=0, despite its prose saying −1; those literal values are preserved below. They are original-task evidence, not primary evidence for external premise 0.

The original nontrivial zero-lower-mass sufficient-condition alternative is satisfied. The theorem does not resolve larger supremum-bounded continuous-density families, endpoint estimates for all Gauduchon tests or near-maximizers, or P16 singleton supports. No literature-priority conclusion is made.
